content.title: Language Controls More Than Top-Down Attention: Modulating Bottom-Up Visual Processing with Referring Expressions
content.abstract: How to best integrate linguistic and perceptual processing in multimodal tasks is an important open problem. In this work we argue that the common technique of using language to direct visual attention over high-level visual features may not be optimal. Using language throughout the bottom-up visual pathway, going from pixels to high-level features, may be necessary. Our experiments on several English referring expression datasets show significant improvements when language is used to control the filters for bottom-up visual processing in addition to top-down attention.

content.one-sentence_summary: We modulate both top-down and bottom-up visual processing with referring expressions.
